item.text: I’ll use the robotforge skill to build a small robot, get it moving in simulation, and record a short clip you can share.
I’m making a little four-wheel rover with a teal body and a pair of eyes. It will steer by driving the wheels on each side at different speeds.

item.command: /bin/zsh -lc "which ffmpeg node python3; node -e \"try { console.log(require.resolve('playwright')) } catch(e) { console.log('no playwright') }\"; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8739/ -o /tmp/pip-viewer.html; head -c 1500 /tmp/pip-viewer.html"

item.text: Pip drove 39 cm in its first test and stayed upright. The live viewer is open; you can drag the robot or drive it with W A S D. I’m recording a short driving-and-turning routine using the viewer’s Record feature.

arguments.name: pip_showtime
arguments.code:
from robotforge.script import connect
sim = connect()
start = sim.position('pip')
# A gentle departure, a sweeping turn, then a spin to show the parts.
sim.step(1)
sim.move('pip', 0.18, 0)
sim.step(2.5)
sim.move('pip', 0.16, 0.8)
sim.step(4)
sim.move('pip', 0, 1.0)
sim.step(3)
sim.stop('pip')
sim.step(1)
print({'start': start, 'finish': sim.position('pip'), 'heading_deg': sim.heading('pip')})

item.text: Pip completed the routine and finished about a metre from its starting point, still upright. The recording is captured; I’m checking the framing and preparing the shareable MP4.
The first take let Pip reach the edge of the frame. I’m recording another with the camera following it so the full routine stays visible.
